title: Japan’s most powerful supercomputer may have been hacked, over 4,000 users’ personal data stolen
summary: Fugaku, Japan's most powerful supercomputer, has suffered a suspected data breach, with the information of more than 4,000 of its users potentially stolen as a result.
body: Fugaku, Japan's most powerful supercomputer and the ninth-fastest on the planet, has suffered a suspected data breach. The news was announced by its operator, Riken, which is the country's national research institute, with the outfit also confirming that personal information relating to more than 4,000 users of Fugaku was potentially taken during the breach. Further, the information of 375 users of Riken's Rikyu AI supercomputer was also possibly taken. The personal information includes names, email addresses, research files, and even the authentication information that was used to access the supercomputers and related services. The Japan Times reports that the operators of Fugaku first became aware of suspicious communications on November 12, with those suspicions then triggering an investigation. By November 14, the investigation had confirmed that unauthorized access to Fugaku had taken place, with access also blocked at that time. The investigation identified that hackers had used the supercomputer's externally accessible operational status dashboard as the springboard for the hack between November 10 and November 13. Now taken offline while security concerns are addressed, th…

The broader goal is to accelerate factory automation, particularly in older fabs, while laying the groundwork for fully autonomous semiconductor manufacturing. title: 403 hyperscale US data centers used staggering 82 terawatts of electricity in a year, more than 80% of Michigan’s entire consumption
summary: A Harvard-led study in Nature Sustainability estimates 403 US hyperscale data centers used about 82 TWh of electricity in a year.
body: A Harvard-led study estimates that 403 hyperscale U.S. data center sites consumed about 82 TWh of electricity in a year, 1.8% of the country’s total, with more than half coming from gas and coal sources, Wired reports . This compares to the entire state of Michigan selling 99 TWh in 2024. The data centers’ pull also put out an estimated 25.7 million metric tons (Mt) of CO2, which is two to three times a 2018 estimate. Hyperscale data centers, in this case, refer to sites run by a hyperscale cloud or content provider, or a colocation operator who serves one, with a capacity in the tens of megawatts. The 675 candidate sites came from data vendor Baxtel, with 403 confirmed with satellite imagery and building-footprint maps, at an average capacity of 39.9 MW and a median of 36 MW. Nobody officially counts what the data centers actually draw from the grid. Instead, the electricity is estimated by multiplying each site’s maximum capacity by the hours in a year and an estimate of how hard the data centers run. For CO2 and the source mix, each site is placed in its grid region, of 23 total in the study, with a regional average mix from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). These are …

title: China engineers behind J-35 fighter jet pioneer 3D-printed load-bearing structures in military aircraft
summary: China's first aircraft research institute and developer of the J-35 fighter jets 3D-printed a primary load-bearing component over 16.4 feet in length, minimizing the need for bolts and speeding up research progress.
body: The Shenyang Aircraft Design and Research Institute, the developers of China’s J-35 fighter jet platform, used metal 3D printing to create large primary load-bearing structures for military aircraft applications. Global Times reports the structure is over 16.4 feet (five meters) in length, using segmented printing and fusion techniques. Shenyang Aircraft Design and Research Institute, a research organization under the Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC), has been working on 3D-printed aircraft components since 2003. The impressively large 3D-printed components are the culmination of decades of research and development of various metal additive manufacturing techniques. The engineers are no strangers to large 3D-printed components : in 2005, they achieved secondary load-bearing structures; then, in 2012, large primary load-bearing titanium alloy structures, earning additive manufacturing expert Wang Huaming and his team China’s National Technological Invention Award. Recently, however, the team created a primary load-bearing structure even larger, at over 16.4 feet. title: China retains fastest supercomputer in the world crown as AI data centers soak up new hardware
summary: The Top 500 list records the fewest new entrants in its history amid a massive shift in compute infrastructure investments towards AI factories.
body: China's LineShine remains the world's highest-performing supercomputer, according to the 68 th edition of the Top500 list published at SC26 in Chicago on Monday. For the first time in decades, the supercomputer ranking saw exceptionally few additions despite unprecedented demand for high-performance computing hardware, as the vast amounts of compute resources deployed these days are destined for artificial intelligence (AI) data centers rather than traditional supercomputers. Top 10 supercomputers unchanged China's LineShine , installed at the National Supercomputer Center in Shenzhen, offers sustained FP64 compute performance of 2.198 FP64 ExaFLOPS in the High Performance Linpack (HPL) benchmark at 42.22 MW. The machine relies on the homegrown LingKun platform with 304-core Armx9-based LX2 processors clocked at 1.55 GHz (13,789,440 cores in total) and the proprietary LingQi interconnect. Unlike the other four exascale-class supercomputers, LineShine does not use any compute accelerators and exclusively relies on CPUs, which is largely why it only gains 3.6X performance when moving from FP64 to mixed-precision data, which is lower than systems that use low-precision accelerators. …

title: Researchers ‘recognize that AI will never replace HPC,’ says AMD executive — high-precision workloads will ‘exist for a very long time’ even as AI usage expands
summary: The emergence of AI has seemingly posed a threat to high-precision FP64 computation, but AMD doesn't think the HPC world is moving away from those complex calculations in the wake of AI.
body: While AI continues to reshape industries across science and mathematics, traditional supercomputing has seemingly taken a back seat. However, AMD's Scott Tease told Tom's Hardware Premium that most HPC sites “recognize that AI will never replace HPC,” and suggests that building a heterogeneous compute stack is the best path forward to tackle bleeding-edge research, despite Nvidia pushing performance on lower-precision data types higher for AI workloads at the cost of native performance for the important double-precision FP64 format that’s critical for HPC workloads. A heterogeneous compute stack brings together quantum, HPC, and AI under one roof, a fleet that AMD is helping pilot at Oak Ridge National Laboratory alongside IBM. Tease is AMD’s corporate vice president of HPC and sovereign AI, who joined the company earlier this year after more than a decade at Lenovo (and, before that, another 13 years at IBM). We spoke with Tease ahead of SC26 to get a read on the state of HPC, how it intersects with AI, and what’s actually driving the research community in a time when computer chips are driving headlines about international espionage plots. title: AMD grabs over 40% of new TOP500 list for supercomputers, up 14% since last year
summary: AMD's Lux supercomputer debuted at position 14 on the new TOP500 list published during SC26. It's one of two machines AMD is developing as part of a $1 billion deal with the U.S. Department of Energy.
body: With the coming of SC26, also comes a fresh edition of the TOP500 list, which ranks the world's most powerful supercomputers. The newly released list illustrates that AMD powers 40% of the list, up 14% compared to 2025. AMD-powered systems now tally up to 202 on the list, up from 177 last year. New to the list is Lux, a “SI + HPC supercomputer” developed by AMD and the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), which debuted at position 14. AMD’s representation in the top 10 is familiar. After debuting in June, China’s LineShine remains in the top slot. El Capitan, powered by AMD chips, is in the second slot, followed by Frontier in third, HPC7 in sixth, and HPC6 in eighth, the same as the most recent TOP500 list. Lux was announced a little over a year ago in a $1 billion deal between the DOE and AMD to develop two supercomputers. This is the first of the two, and the first time it’s been on the TOP500. The system was built by HPE and developed by AMD and DOE as part of the U.S. government’s Genesis Mission. The machine is housed in Oak Ridge National Laboratory’s Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility (OLCF), alongside machines like Frontier. Lux relies on over 4,000 Instinct MI355X GPUs …

title: Intel bets on Classiq acquisition to turn Quantum efforts into commercially viable business
summary: Intel aims to turn its quantum computing research effort into a commercial business by combining its silicon spin-qubit technology and manufacturing capabilities with Classiq’s established software platform and customer base.
body: After having spent more than a decade pursuing quantum computing research, Intel is making its first real push at commercializing its efforts. First, with the pending acquisition of quantum computing company Classiq, which has an existing list of enterprise customers. Intel says it'll be the only company that can produce qubit chips and cryogenic control electronics at scale; the deal would give it a complete top-to-bottom hardware-to-software stack, and Intel will also gain the chance to become a leading vendor of quantum computing products. Intel's acquisition of Classiq is expected to complete in the first half of 2027. The key ingredient of that strategy is the pending acquisition of Classiq , which offers a hardware-agnostic quantum software development platform that enables engineers to design, synthesize, optimize, simulate, and execute quantum algorithms using high-level programming tools and AI-assisted automation, essentially untying software design from the complexity of quantum hardware. title: Minisforum Elite Mini M2 Air-304 review: A quiet and compact Wildcat
summary: With an Intel Wildcat Lake CPU, the Minisforum Elite Mini M2 Air-304 PC runs cool and quiet, but is only suitable for casual users. Due to the prices of RAM and storage, trying to save money using entry-level silicon doesn’t work as well as it used to.
body: Minisforum’s Intel-based M2 line includes mini PCs with powerful processors such as the Core Ultra X7 Processor 358H (with 16C/16T CPU and B390 graphics), and the Core Ultra 7 356H (16C/16T). But there are more modest systems, too. The M2 Air-304 here is the most affordable option, based around the Intel Core 3 processor 304 with its 5C/5T CPU (1x Cougar Cove P-core and 4x Darkmont LP E-cores) and an iGPU with just a single Xe3 core. No surprise, the little brother in the pack, both in terms of physical size and computing resources, is the most affordable. It currently starts at $263 for a barebones version. However, our test sample with 16GB DDR5-5600, a 500GB SSD, and Windows 11 Pro is listed at $559 - direct. That’s an introductory price, and Minisforum’s small text threatens that our configuration will bump up to $699 at some point in the future. Such a rise would put this product offering on very shaky ground, and we see B&H Photo has already raised the price at $729. Overall, this Mini PC was pleasant to use, though. title: Anthropic says Claude Mythos Preview cut AMD MI355X onboarding from up to 12 months to around three days
summary: Anthropic says Claude Mythos Preview brought up prompt processing for one model on AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs in about three days.
body: Anthropic told IPO investors that its Claude Mythos Preview model did the software work required to get its AI running on AMD’s GPUs in about three days, with “basically no human intervention,” a job it says used to take six to 12 months. The three days cover prompt processing for one Anthropic model on AMD MI355X GPUs “at a useful level of performance,” with Mythos porting or writing “almost 100% of the kernels.” That kind of low-level code, which ties an AI model to one company’s chips, has long been part of Nvidia’s CUDA moat, and an AI that can write it in days would suggest that moat is eroding. Tom Brown, Anthropic’s co-founder and chief compute officer, made the time comparison, noting to investors that the original meant using a team of “dozens of engineers.” The company already runs its models on multiple kinds of chips — on GPUs from Nvidia and AMD, Google’s TPUs, and AWS Trainium — and its fleet is managed as “one fungible pool of compute.” Brown called the early multi-chip decision “an unconventional bet.” It may have been a wise one, given that Google’s TPUs can now natively run AI models built in PyTorch , and Meta uses them in production. title: Overlocker uses vibecoded BIOS modification to target Intel's non-K overclocking restrictions
summary: ASRock discontinued SkyOC following Intel's efforts to block non-K CPU overclocking, but an enthusiast is now using AI to see if the old workaround can be adapted for newer platforms.
body: In an attempt to resurrect ASRock's discontinued SkyOC overclocking feature, an enthusiast has vibe-coded a motherboard BIOS using AI, potentially bringing non-K CPU overclocking to modern Intel CPUs. According to a post on X, Hardware 360º used Chat-GPT Astra to decompile and compare two versions of an ASRock BIOS, one released with SkyOC and another with the feature disabled. The AI reportedly identified the code responsible for enabling the overclocking workaround and modified it to create a BIOS ready for implementation on a compatible motherboard. Unfortunately, it remains to be seen whether the modified firmware can restore SkyOC on modern Intel platforms, as the workaround is yet to be fully tested. For context, Intel offers multiplier-based overclocking only on its unlocked K-series processors like the Core i9-14900K and the newer Core Ultra 270K Plus . Non-K models have locked multipliers, which restrict users from pushing CPU frequencies. However, there’s another way to raise the speed of a processor by pushing the base clock itself. body: Amazon has suffered a major setback in its plans to offer a viable Starlink rival, after 40 satellites destined for low Earth orbit (LEO) were destroyed. title: Jailbroken PS4 runs 9-billion-parameter AI model at up to 43 tokens per second
summary: Garlic LLM runs Alibaba’s Qwen3.5-9B on a jailbroken PlayStation 4’s GPU, fully offline, at 31 to 39 tokens per second.
body: Developer Leonardo Alegría’s open-source project Garlic LLM lets a jailbroken PS4 run the 9-billion-parameter Qwen3.5-9B AI model offline on the console’s 2013-era GPU. The app talks to the GPU directly, and the model is shrunk to about 4.5GiB to fit in the console’s memory, running at 31 to 39 tokens per second. The project, named after the memory the GPU reads directly — its sibling memory type is “Onion” — relies on a PS4 running GoldHEN, which is a homebrew enabler for exploited consoles. Garlic LLM is a free, single 5.66GB download, available on Hugging Face and installable through the PS4’s Package Installer, with about 6GB free needed, or 12GB if the package is first copied to the console’s internal disk. The developer tested it on a base/Slim PS4 on firmware 11.52. (Image credit: Leonardo Alegría/Garlic LLM) It’s capable of voice conversation, with spoken replies in seven languages through the Chatterbox speech model and the chat model running at about 22 tokens per second. A held controller button also lets it take dictation with Nvidia’s Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 speech-to-text model, which supports 25 European languages. title: Jensen Huang could be plotting return as Nvidia CEO, report claims
summary: Jensen Huang could be back in his old Nvidia office soon as allies rally to push the AI chipmaker to take him back just days after he was ousted over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
body: Just days after he left the company under a cloud of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy, former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang might be on his way back to the company he founded. That's after a number of his allies rallied in support for Huang, including influential SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and outspoken Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney. The pair are just two of those demanding that Nvidia's board has a rethink, hoping that it will choose to "Bring Jensen Back" to the company. Huang is now discussing that possibility, according to a Financial Times report . "Huang has discussed with confidantes the possibility of returning, according to multiple people familiar with the matter," the report claimed, adding that allies were putting together a "war room" of Silicon Valley figures to try and lobby for his return. Huang's resignation from his Nvidia post came after he released a statement confirming his affair , one which could have repercussions far beyond Nvidia itself. U.S. intelligence was reported to believe that the woman involved in an affair with Jensen Huang, Alice Huang (no relation), is a spy working for the Chinese Ministry of State Security , or MSS. title: Fable 5.2 creates an underwater world in a browser in only 96 KB
summary: Fable 5.2 creates an underwater world in a browser in only 96 KB — impressive demo shows how far agent agency has come
body: Claude Fable 5.2 was released recently to mostly rave reviews, with both users and analysis outlets ranking it nipping at the heels of the much pricier Opus 5.5. Perhaps as practical proof of that claim, front-end developer Maksymilian Dendura took inspiration from the demoscene and had Fable roll his own virtual underwater world, Abyssal Garden , in only 96 KB of Javascript/HTML — you can check it out here . The demo's 3D space and textures are all procedurally generated, meaning they're the result of mathematical equations rather than prebuilt 3D meshes, and all calculated on load. Using actual meshes and images for textures would otherwise take up a significant amount of space. Building structures procedurally is difficult and has limitations, but it's exceedingly effective when used properly. Some games employ this technique for repeated elements like trees and grass. Likewise, all the visual effects and even some texturing are done with shaders, which are small programs that change how a mesh or texture appears — for example, to make parts of an object shiny. body: Without a doubt, Nvidia's dominance in the AI hardware market stems not only from the capabilities of its AI accelerators and its vast software ecosystem, but also from its aggressive procurement strategy that effectively denies its rivals access to sufficient production capacity at TSMC and other contractors. The result of his deals is that supply and capacity commitments rose by almost a quarter of a trillion dollars in a single quarter, primarily due to memory procurement, according to SemiAnalysis. However, even Nvidia's former chief executive Jensen Huang had apparently begun to question the sustainability of this strategy before his departure, based on reports from The Wall Street Journal and SemiAnalysis . Over the past several years, Nvidia has not only captured the vast majority of the AI accelerator market, but has also secured a substantial proportion of the world's production capacity for advanced logic, high-bandwidth memory (HBM), and various other components required to build AI accelerators and systems, which has limited the ability of its competitors to ramp up shipments of their processors. title: Developer creates a 100% valid ZIP file that doubles as a BIOS-bootable operating system
summary: Crafty techie concocts ZIP that's simultaneously a valid archive, BIOS-bootable, and a Multiboot image
body: Hacking stories these days mostly involve someone using an army of AI agents to find vulnerabilities in networks and software that were carefully hidden in plain sight. Today, for a change, we have a story about hacking in its original meaning — twisting computing artifacts into purposes not in their design spec. David Oberhollenzer, aka Goliath, a greybeard in spirit if not in shade, crafted a 100% valid ZIP file that's simultaneously an archive, BIOS-bootable, and a Multiboot-compatible OS image. You can unpack the ZIP file just like any other, boot it using Linux's GRUB, QEMU, or any other Multiboot-compatible loader (even if imaged to different media), or alternatively, perform the finest party trick: image-write it to a floppy and boot from it directly from BIOS on any compatible PC, without modification. Much like me, that sequence of words may be triggering a head-tilt reminiscent of a confused puppy, so we'll explain. The first thing you need to know is that unlike most file types, the metadata (in this case, file directory) of a ZIP is actually at the end of the archive. summary: Dai's post shows how much Nvidia employees looked up to the former CEO.
body: Just days after Jensen Huang suddenly resigned from his position at Nvidia , an Nvidia Robot Research Engineer said that he would leave the company as well. But more than just showing support for the former CEO with a generic “I stand with Jensen” message, Darrel Dai laid out several reasons for the decision on X . I’ve decided to leave NVIDIA. There are a few things I want to say.As a robotics engineer at NVIDIA, I have seen Jensen as much more than the company’s CEO.I admire his willingness to invest in a future that was not yet obvious. He committed to CUDA long before the deep learning boom and positioned NVIDIA for AI before it became everyone’s priority. Those decisions helped build the infrastructure that powers today’s AI.I have seen that same vision in physical AI: investing in robotics, sharing open-source tools and projects, and building computing platforms that bring AI into the physical world. This is the work I do every day—and a future I believe in.But what matters most to me is the culture he helped build.Engineers are encouraged to explore, take risks, and learn from mistakes.
